title: Learning to recover: Adaptive local branching with reinforcement learning for log-truck routing and scheduling under disruptions
summary: We consider the real-time reoptimisation of log-truck routing and scheduling in the Canadian forestry industry following unforeseen disruptions. Road closures, vehicle breakdowns, travel delays, and demand fluctuations invalidate pre-established tactical plans and call for recovery decisions that simultaneously restore feasibility and limit deviation from the original schedule, two objectives inherently in tension under tight time constraints.
